name: Stereotyping
description: People use category labels to fill in missing information about others, inferring traits or expectations from group membership rather than individual evidence. This can speed judgment, but it also distorts perception and decision-making.
design_relevance_note: Central to inclusive design, persona construction, safety systems, recommendation logic, and research interpretation. Designers can accidentally encode category shortcuts into copy, segmentation, moderation, or model outputs.
prevalence_note: A widely recognized term in inclusive-design, fairness, trust-and-safety, and user-research discourse, even if it is less central in baseline interaction-design heuristic lists.

findings.description: Classic experimental social-perception evidence showed that observers can over-infer a relationship between group membership and behavior from distinctive pairings, even when the underlying data do not warrant that association. This is the core illusory-correlation pattern: salient co-occurrence gets mistaken for real correlation.
findings.source_title: Illusory correlation in interpersonal perception: A cognitive basis of stereotypic judgments

findings.description: Reviewing social-cognition research, Macrae and Bodenhausen argue that perceivers routinely use social categories to simplify person perception. Category activation shapes trait inference and impression formation, and cognitive control only partly constrains these stereotypic inferences.
findings.source_title: Social Cognition: Thinking Categorically about Others

applications.title: A Jena University preschool program reduced children's early stereotyping through increased intergroup contact
applications.description: Researchers at Jena University, led by Dr. Andreas Beelmann, developed a program for pre-school-aged children that increases their contact with children from different social, ethnic, or gender groups -- aiming to prevent a natural in-group-favoring bias from developing into stereotyping and prejudice against other groups later in life.
applications.ethical_note: A genuinely prosocial application of behavioral research, not a designed influence on a user for commercial gain -- relevant to any platform or product design context (education technology, children's media, community/social features) that has an opportunity to structure early intergroup contact rather than reinforce in-group-only social defaults.
